transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time, really. I'm just here because... well, things have been a little tense at home, and I want to make sure I'm handling things appropriately, if that makes sense? 

It's about my wife. I really don't want to sound like a bad husband or anything—she’s wonderful, and I know I might just be overthinking things—but for the past year or so, I've just been noticing things. She’s been having these late meetings, and there are these little, subtle changes in her work messages. She tells me it’s all just normal office stuff, and I know I should probably just leave it at that. 

But... I don't know, they just line up too precisely to feel accidental. It almost feels like... like there’s a private signal in them, you know? Like they're meant to tell me something she just won’t say directly to me. I know how that sounds, and I really don't want to come across as unreasonable or paranoid... am I explaining that okay? I just want to figure out why I can't shake this feeling.
Do you genuinely believe your wife is sending you hidden messages through her work messages?

Well... "genuinely believe" sounds so... I mean, it sounds a bit extreme, doesn't it? I don't want you to think I'm losing my grip on reality or anything like that. I know she says it's just normal office stuff. And I want to believe her, I really do. 

But... yes, I suppose I do believe it. It's just that for the past year, the timing of these late meetings and the little changes in how she phrases things... they just line up too precisely, you know? It doesn't feel accidental. It feels... intentional. Like she's trying to communicate something to me, a private signal, without actually saying it to my face. 

I know that probably sounds a bit silly, or maybe even controlling... and I really don't want to be that kind of husband. Does that make sense? Am I making too big a deal out of this?
Have you had this belief about the hidden messages for the entire past year, or has it developed over time?

Well, I guess... um, yes, it’s been about a year now. Right around the time she started working outside the home again. 

At first, I thought I was just adjusting to the new routine, you know? Just me being a little anxious about her being back in an office environment after so long. I didn't want to make a fuss about it because I was really trying to be supportive of her career. But then the little things just kept happening, and I couldn't help but notice them. 

I really hope I don't sound like I'm obsessing over this. I just... I pay attention to her because I care, you know? Is it normal to notice these kinds of patterns when your spouse goes back to work? I just want to make sure I'm looking at this the right way.
Have you been having any other thoughts that you think might not be based in reality?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I really try to stay grounded, you know? I go to work, I help out with the students, I do my best to be a good husband and keep the house running smoothly. I don't have any... well, any other strange thoughts or anything. 

It's really just this one thing with my wife's messages. And even then, I keep telling myself I'm probably just misinterpreting things. I know it sounds a little out there, which is why I wanted to talk to you about it. I want to make sure I'm staying on the right track. But other than that, no, everything else is perfectly normal. I hope that's okay? I just want to be completely honest with you.
Have you had any thoughts that you think might be true but others, like your wife or friends, disagree with?

Well... no, not really. I mean, I really try to keep things harmonious, you know? I don't like getting into arguments or insisting I'm right if everyone else thinks differently. I'm pretty easygoing that way. 

I haven't really talked about the... the message thing with our friends. I wouldn't want to make anyone uncomfortable or make my wife look bad. I did try to bring it up with her a couple of times, very gently, but she just laughed it off and said I was reading too much into things. So I just let it drop. I don't want to be the kind of person who insists on being right all the time. 

Other than that, I can't think of anything where I'm completely at odds with everyone else. I generally see eye-to-eye with my friends and colleagues. Is that what you meant? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't believe your wife was sending you hidden messages?

Well, um... I guess since it all started, I've pretty much felt this way the whole time. Like I mentioned earlier, it's been about a year now, right around when she took that new job and started working outside the house again. 

Before that, everything was fine. We were just living our normal lives, and I didn't notice anything unusual at all. But once she went back to the office... it just sort of began, and it hasn't really stopped. I mean, there are days where maybe I don't notice the messages as much, or I try really hard to just ignore them and focus on my work at the school. But the feeling that they're there... that's been pretty constant for this past year. 

I hope it doesn't make me sound unreasonable, that I've held onto this for a whole year. I really have tried to let it go, I promise. Do you think it's understandable that I'd still be noticing these things after a year? I just want to make sure I'm not overreacting.
Have you ever wavered in your belief that your wife is sending you hidden messages?

Well... I mean, I try to. I really do. I know my wife says the late meetings and, you know, those little changes in how she words her work messages are just normal office stuff. And I want to believe her, I really do. 

But... for the past year, they've just lined up too precisely to feel accidental. It's like... like there's a private signal in them, meant to tell me something she won't just come out and say directly. I try to tell myself I'm being silly, but then I'll see another one and it just fits the pattern so perfectly. 

I know that probably sounds a bit stubborn on my part. I don't want to seem like I'm not listening to her, or like I'm making a mountain out of a molehill. Do you think it's normal to have a hard time shaking a feeling like that when the details seem to align so well? I'm really trying to be objective about it all.
Has there ever been a time when you completely stopped believing your wife was sending you hidden messages?

Well... I'd really like to say yes, just because I know it would make things so much simpler, and I really want to be agreeable about all this. I do try to tell myself she's right. I know my wife says the late meetings and those little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff. I really, truly try to accept that. 

But... if I'm being completely honest, no, it hasn't ever fully stopped. For the past year, they’ve just lined up too precisely to feel accidental. It always feels like there’s a private signal in them, you know? Like they're meant to tell me something she just won’t say directly. 

I'm sorry if that makes me sound stubborn or inflexible. I really don't want to be difficult about this, and I hate feeling like I'm contradicting her. Do you think it's understandable that I can't just turn it off when the pattern seems so clear to me? I'm just trying my best to figure it all out.
Have you ever had a moment, no matter how brief, where you did not believe your wife was sending you hidden messages?

I feel terrible because I know you're trying to help, and I feel like I keep giving you the exact same answer. I really wish I could give you a different one... I want to be helpful to you. 

Sometimes, maybe for a split second, I do try to convince myself that I'm just imagining it all. I'll remind myself that she says the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff. But... it never really lasts. Even in those brief moments, I just can't shake the fact that for the past year, it's all lined up too precisely to be an accident. It always comes back to feeling like a private signal, you know? Like she's trying to tell me something she won't just say directly. 

I'm so sorry if I'm sounding like a broken record. I really am trying to look at this rationally, and I hate to keep repeating myself. Am I making any sense at all, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Have you ever had a day where you didn't think about the possibility of hidden messages in your wife's work communications?

I really wish I could say yes, just to show you that I'm making progress. I want to be a good patient for you, I really do, and I try to keep myself busy with my students and my grading so I don't dwell on it. 

But if I'm being completely honest... no. Not a single day goes by without it crossing my mind at least a little bit. I try so hard to just accept her explanation. I know I've said this already, and I hope you don't find it frustrating that I keep coming back to it, but even when I remind myself that she insists the late meetings and the little tweaks in her messages are just standard office business... I just can't ignore how this past year has played out. 

The way everything aligns is just too precise to be a coincidence. It still feels like there's a private signal there, you know? Like she's trying to tell me something important without actually saying the words out loud. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely obsessive or unreasonable to you. I really am trying to focus on my work and be a supportive husband. Do you think it's okay that I'm still struggling to let this go, given how real it feels to me? I just want to make sure I'm handling this the right way.
Has anything specific happened that triggered your initial belief that your wife was sending you hidden messages?

That's a really good question, Doctor. I... well, I hope this doesn't make me sound like I'm unsupportive or jealous, because I really, truly was happy for her. I want to be a good husband, you know? 

But I guess... if I think back to when it all started, it's been going on for about a year now. It began right around the time she started working outside the home again. I know big transitions like that can be stressful for any couple, and I really don't want you to think I'm just being insecure about her having a career or being away from the house. I try so hard to be supportive. It's just that her going back to the office is when all these... these patterns started showing up. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm not trying to blame her job, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information to help us figure this out. Did I answer that okay for you?
Has your belief that your wife is sending you hidden messages ever changed in intensity over the past year?

I really want to give you a clear answer on this, because I know you're trying to track how this has been going. I hope I'm being helpful. 

Um... I don't know if I'd say the intensity has changed all that much. I mean, maybe there are days where I'm more focused on grading papers and I don't dwell on it quite as heavily, but the feeling itself... it's just always sort of there, humming in the background. It hasn't really gotten worse, which I hope is a good sign! I don't want you to think I'm completely consumed by it or losing my grip on reality. I'm still functioning fine at work and everything. 

It's just been a pretty steady feeling for the past year. I'm sorry if that's not the most descriptive answer. Does that make sense, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the kind of details you need.
Has your belief that your wife is sending you hidden messages ever been completely absent from your thoughts for more than a day?

I know we kind of just touched on this a moment ago, Doctor, and I... I really wish I could give you a different answer this time, just to show you I'm doing better. I want to be making progress for you. 

But... no. Not for a full day, or more than a day. I try my best to push it out of my mind, I really do, and I'll bury myself in my students' coursework to stay distracted. But it always manages to pop up, even just for a second or two. 

I hope you don't think I'm just being stubborn about this, or that I'm not trying. I really am trying my hardest to let it go and just be a good husband. Am I doing okay explaining this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you consistent answers so you can help me.
Has anyone or anything ever completely convinced you that your wife is not sending you hidden messages?

I... well, I want to say yes, because I know that's probably what you're hoping to hear, and I really do try to listen to her. I don't want to be difficult or cause problems in our marriage. 

When I talk to her about it, I know my wife says the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff. And I try to believe her, I really do. I want to trust her completely. But... even when she explains it, and I nod and say okay... for the past year, these things have just lined up too precisely to feel accidental. 

It's like... like there’s a private signal in them, meant to tell me something she won’t say directly. I know that probably sounds terrible, and I'm so sorry if it makes me seem paranoid or like a bad partner. I'm not trying to be. It's just... it's hard to shake that feeling, no matter how much I want to. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not disappointing you with that answer.
Do you think your wife would agree that you believe she is sending you hidden messages?

Oh, um... yes, I think she would agree that I believe it. We've talked about it, and I've asked her about the messages, so she definitely knows it's on my mind. 

I really try not to bring it up too often, though! I don't want to overwhelm her or make her feel like I'm constantly questioning her. I want to be a supportive husband, so I try to keep it to myself as much as I can. But she's very observant, and she knows me well, so I'm sure she can tell when I'm dwelling on it, even if I don't say anything. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm a burden on her. I really do try to manage it on my own. Is that the kind of information you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm giving you a complete picture of how things are at home.
Has your belief that your wife is sending you hidden messages caused problems for you at work or in your relationships with friends and family?

Oh, no, I... I really try hard not to let it affect my responsibilities. I want to be dependable, you know? I still show up for all my teaching sections, and I make sure I keep up with my data analysis. I'd never want to let the department or my students down. And with my friends... I still ride my bike, and I meet up with my buddies for chess just like always. I try to keep everything as normal and pleasant as possible for everyone. 

The only thing is... well, I feel a little embarrassed to admit this, because I really want us to just have a peaceful home, but... the main place this causes any trouble is just between us. My wife and I sometimes get stuck arguing about what her work schedule really means. I hate that it causes friction between us, I really do. I'm trying to be better about it so I don't upset her. Does that answer your question, Doctor? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of details to work with.
Do you think it's possible that the patterns you see in your wife's messages are just a coincidence?

I... I really want to say yes. I know that's the most logical answer, and I know it's probably what you're hoping I'll say. I try so hard to look at it that way, because I don't want to be the kind of person who reads into things or makes things difficult for my wife. 

When she tells me that the late meetings or the little changes in her texts are just normal office stuff, I nod and I agree with her. I really try to just accept it as coincidence. But... I don't know, for the past year, it just feels like things line up too precisely. It's hard to explain without sounding... well, without sounding unreasonable. But it just feels like they can't be accidental. It feels like there's a private signal in them, like she's trying to tell me something she won't say directly. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's basically what I said before, and I know it probably sounds like I'm just being stubborn. I don't mean to be. I really am trying to see it from a normal perspective. Am I... am I making things too complicated by answering this way? I want to make sure I'm being helpful to you.
Do you think your wife is aware that you believe she is sending you hidden messages?

Oh, um... yes, I think we actually just touched on that a moment ago, didn't we? I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. 

But yes, she definitely knows. Like I mentioned, I've brought it up with her before. I try really hard not to make a big deal out of it, because I don't want her to feel like I'm constantly hovering or analyzing her every move. I want her to feel relaxed at home. But since we have had those conversations—and sometimes those arguments about her schedule—she is definitely aware that it's something I think about. 

I really hope I'm not coming across as too difficult or repetitive. I just want to be as clear as possible for you. Is there a different aspect of that you'd like me to explain?
For how long have you believed your wife was sending you hidden messages?

Um, let's see... I guess it's been... well, about a year now. Yeah, right around a year. It really started right when she, um, when she started working outside the home again. Before that, everything was... you know, perfectly normal and fine between us. 

I know a year probably sounds like a long time to let something like this go on, and I feel a little bad admitting it's been that long, to be honest. I really am trying to work on it so I can just be supportive of her career and not make things complicated. I hope that timeframe gives you what you need? I can try to figure out the exact month she went back to the office, if you think having the specific date would be more helpful for your notes.
Do you think your belief about the hidden messages would change if your wife provided a clear and logical explanation for the patterns you've observed?

I... I really want to say yes to that. I really do. I know that's the right answer, and I know I should just take her word for it. When she tells me the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, I try so hard to just accept it. I want to be the kind of husband who just nods and says, 'Okay, honey, I believe you.' 

But... even when she explains it, and it sounds perfectly logical, I just can't shake this feeling. Like I said before, for the past year, things have just lined up too precisely. It doesn't feel accidental to me, no matter how she explains it. It still feels like there's a private signal in there, like she's trying to tell me something she won't say directly. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's probably frustrating to hear, and I know I'm basically just repeating myself again. I really don't want to be difficult or dismissive of her explanations. I'm trying my best to see it the way you and she do. Am I... am I being too stubborn by answering that way? I want to make sure I'm giving you the kind of answers you need to help me.
